recent_posts.title: Microservices design patterns explained with an e-commerce example
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of core microservices design patterns using an e-commerce platform as a running example. Covers the motivation for splitting a monolith, database-per-service pattern, service discovery (client-side vs server-side), load balancing algorithms, synchronous vs asynchronous communication (REST vs message brokers like Kafka), resilience patterns (circuit breaker, exponential backoff with jitter, idempotency keys), and observability through centralized logging with trace IDs and distributed tracing tools like Jaeger.

recent_posts.title: How a MongoDB migration script corrupted 2 million records in production
recent_posts.summary: A migration script to encrypt sensitive user data in MongoDB corrupted over 2 million records by accidentally wiping out unencrypted fields. The bug occurred because MongoDB's $set operation replaces entire nested objects rather than merging properties. Running the migration twice resulted in both encrypted and unencrypted fields being set to undefined, causing queries to return millions of records and spike memory usage in Kubernetes pods. Recovery required restoring a database backup from before the migration and cross-referencing with Redshift data to identify users who registered during the incident window.

recent_posts.title: How Figma scaled their PostgreSQL database to support 10 million users
recent_posts.summary: Figma scaled from a single PostgreSQL database to a horizontally sharded architecture supporting 10 million users. The journey involved three phases: immediate relief through vertical scaling, read replicas, and connection pooling; medium-term stability via logical partitioning of table groups into dedicated databases; and long-term scalability through horizontal sharding with a custom query router. Key innovations included optimized logical replication by removing indexes during migration, two-phase deployment using PG Bouncer for safe routing changes, logical sharding with PostgreSQL views for testing before physical splits, and a custom Golang DB proxy for intelligent query routing across shards.

recent_posts.title: Uber migrates from DynamoDB to custom MySQL database saving $6M annually
recent_posts.summary: Uber reduced database costs by $6 million annually by migrating their financial transaction system from DynamoDB to DocStore, their custom MySQL-based distributed database. The migration involved building LedgerStore 2.0 with immutable records, data integrity guarantees, and solving hot partition problems through deterministic sharding. The process included careful data backfilling, shadow writes for real-time sync, and dual read validation to ensure zero downtime during the transition.

recent_posts.title: Discord's journey scaling message search from billions to trillions using Elasticsearch and Kubernetes
recent_posts.summary: Discord scaled their message search infrastructure from billions to trillions of messages by evolving from a single Elasticsearch cluster to a cell-based architecture using Kubernetes. They solved performance issues through bulk indexing with message queues, implemented load-aware shard allocation, and replaced their custom queue system with Google Pub/Sub for guaranteed message delivery. The redesign included specialized node types, dedicated cells for large servers, and enabled new features like cross-DM search.

recent_posts.title: How Nvidia Reduced JSON Processing Costs by Over 80%
recent_posts.summary: Nvidia developed RAPIDS Accelerator to optimize JSON processing in Apache Spark by leveraging GPU parallel processing instead of traditional CPU methods. They overcame initial GPU challenges including cache thrashing, thread divergence, and sparse data patterns through query grouping, lexicographic sorting, and parallel tokenization techniques, achieving over 75% performance improvement and 80% cost reduction for processing terabytes of JSON data.

recent_posts.title: How Neon Postgres manages 750,000+ Databases
recent_posts.summary: Neon addresses PostgreSQL's monolithic architecture limitations by separating compute from storage. Traditional PostgreSQL requires upgrading entire instances for more processing power or storage, leading to over-provisioning and scaling challenges. Neon's serverless architecture uses compute nodes that scale independently, safekeepers for reliable WAL streaming with consensus algorithms, and pageservers that manage data through delta and image layers. The system supports storage sharding across multiple pageservers and enables instant database branching without data duplication, similar to Git branches. This architecture allows for better resource utilization, cost efficiency, and powerful development workflows with isolated database environments.

recent_posts.title: Learning code based animation transformed my content creation journey
recent_posts.summary: A developer shares their year-long journey of learning code-based animation using Motion Canvas to create faceless YouTube content. Starting from basic shapes and movements, they overcame imposter syndrome and built confidence through consistent practice. The story emphasizes that you don't need perfect credentials or timing to start creating - just the willingness to begin with small, imperfect steps.

recent_posts.title: How Instagram Reduced Web Page Load by 50%
recent_posts.summary: Instagram achieved a 50% reduction in feed page load time through multiple optimization strategies. They implemented resource prefetching with proper prioritization, used requestIdleCallback for infinite feed optimization, employed HTTP chunk transfer encoding to stream GraphQL query results alongside HTML, and built a Git-inspired staging system for client-side caching. Additional improvements came from focusing on uncompressed JavaScript size rather than compressed size, implementing inline requirements for module loading, and serving different ES5/ES2017 bundles based on browser capabilities.

recent_posts.title: System design fundamentals for scalable distributed systems
recent_posts.summary: System design fundamentals for building scalable distributed systems, covering key concepts like horizontal vs vertical scaling, the CAP theorem, load balancing strategies, caching mechanisms, SQL vs NoSQL trade-offs, database indexing, and data partitioning techniques including consistent hashing. Explains how to evolve from a simple web server setup to a robust architecture capable of handling millions of users.
